proposed.sourceName: American Halal Foundation (AHF) — 'Are Mono Diglycerides Halal?' (Azmi Anees)
proposed.paraphrase: AHF holds that animal-derived E471 is halal ONLY if from a fully halal-certified (zabiha) animal with documentation and segregated storage; non-zabiha beef or pork-derived E471 is not halal. With source undisclosed, the zabiha-conscious consumer cannot confirm Islamic slaughter, so AHF advises avoiding E471 unless labeled vegetable or halal-certified.

proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa, Jaamia Madinatul Uloom (Trinidad) — 'Is Mono and di-glycerides (E471) permissible?' (Mufti Arshad Ali)
proposed.paraphrase: The fatwa rules animal-derived E471 impermissible unless the animal was slaughtered according to Islamic law, and directs Muslims to avoid mono/diglycerides unless labeled 100% vegetable — a stance that, for undisclosed origin, means the zabiha position avoids E471 absent proof of valid slaughter.

researcherNote: E471 seeded zabiha = grade 4 (Questionable — widely avoided). The strict zabiha position requires proof of Islamic slaughter; undisclosed origin cannot supply it, and animal source could be non-zabiha beef or pork — so the position widely avoids it. Both tier-1 sources directly support avoidance absent zabiha certification. Two independent sources. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
